key_insight: Separating radar-state prediction from language alignment improves radar-to-text retrieval without degrading continuous physical-state estimates.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports privacy-preserving motion and scene monitoring during sensor blackouts and through visual obstructions, though fracture or material-damage assessment is not demonstrated.
method: Encode radar streams with a dual-scale RF encoder and clock anchor feeding an LLM with approximately 3% LoRA adaptation.
Learn continuous states using two-step EMA-JEPA denoising and rollout, plus Batch-VICReg, to predict 3 seconds ahead.
Freeze the physical backbone and train a stop-gradient language-alignment head with false-negative masking.
evidence_signal: On 4,541 radar windows across three domains against 10 baselines, the decoupled head increased radar-to-text R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% while preserving physical readouts, including 3.37° torso-tilt error at a 3-second blackout horizon.
watch_item: Blackout-prediction gains vary by LLM family and representation, so transfer to new sensors and engineering monitoring tasks needs validation.
paper_title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
